Subject: Recap + ask: procurement path and approval owners (Clarise)

Hi Amelia — thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can map the commercial path clearly: 

Recap (quick):
- Use case: customer support triage + internal knowledge base embedding; target first-phase seats: 30 agents, 6 months POC
- Success criteria: <20% escalation rate, average handle time reduction 10–15%
- Timeline: procurement evaluation in Feb, PO or credit-card payment by mid‑March if approved

Requests / next steps:
1) Procurement path: can you confirm whether Clarise prefers issuing a PO (net 30) or paying by card for POCs < $50k?
2) Approval owners: please list the economic buyer, finance reviewer, and contract signatory (name + role + email). If you prefer, we can send a short internal template to capture the approval ladder.
3) Marketplace: are you interested in deploying via AWS Marketplace/your internal marketplace? That affects invoicing and tax forms.

I've attached a short procurement checklist and a draft SOW template we usually start with (attachment stubs below). If it helps, happy to schedule a 20‑minute run-through with your procurement team next week.

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood-SOW-template.pdf (SOW skeleton, editable)
- Clarise-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (procurement fields we typically need)

Thanks — I’ll follow up in two days if I don’t hear back.

Best,
Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the note and the helpful materials. Quick answers below: 

1) Payment method: For POCs under $50k we typically accept card, but anything over $25k often routes to procurement for a PO. This one is borderline — I will confirm with procurement.
2) Approval owners (current):
- Economic buyer: Miguel Santos, VP Product (miguel.santos@clarisehealth.com)
- Finance sponsor: Leila Park, Sr. Manager, Finance (leila.park@clarisehealth.com) — finance reviews T&Cs and budget commitments
- Legal / Signatory: contracts are routed to our GC team (we usually have a delegated signatory, intent to confirm who will sign for sub‑$100k deals)

3) Marketplace: we prefer procurement-managed billing; AWS Marketplace would be easier for finance but requires additional tax setup. We are open to it if Redwood can provide marketplace pricing and terms.

I’ve looped procurement on this thread (procurement@clarisehealth.com) — they will confirm PO thresholds and the delegated signatory.

Thanks,
Amelia
Director, Strategic Programs
Clarise Health

Hannah — procurement here. Confirming the quick details you asked for: 

- PO threshold: Clarise issues POs for any commitment > $30k. For POCs under $30k we accept company card (corporate card) or a short pay‑by‑invoice with preapproval.
- Delegated signatory: For deals <= $50k the Finance Director (Leila Park) can sign; above $50k the GC signs.
- Payment terms: Net 30 on POs; card transactions processed immediately.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred if vendor can provide an offer there; otherwise our procurement team will process a vendor invoice.
